```markdown
<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

164	### 4.2 size 预算参数：image_processor 与 video_processor 的分治
165	
166	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
167	
168	processor 级预算写在两个 `size` 字典里，**图像与视频语义不同**是本节最大的坑：
169	
170	- `processor.image_processor.size = {"longest_edge": ..., "shortest_edge": ...}`
171	  - `longest_edge` 对应 `max_pixels`：**单张图**的 \( H \times W \) 上限；
172	  - `shortest_edge` 对应 `min_pixels`：单张图像素下限（[README.md:L341-L342](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L341-L342)）。
173	- `processor.video_processor.size = {"longest_edge": ..., "shortest_edge": ...}`
174	  - `longest_edge` 是**全部帧的像素总和**上限：视频形状为 \( T \times H \times W \) 时，\( T \times H \times W \) 不得超过它；`shortest_edge` 是总预算下限（[README.md:L345-L346](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L345-L346)）。
175	
176	它与 u2-l2 元素级预算构成**两层旋钮**：
177	
178	| 层次 | 写在哪 | 作用域 | 生效路径 |
179	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
180	| 元素级 `min_pixels` / `max_pixels` / `total_pixels` | messages 的 image/video 元素里 | 单个输入 | qwen-vl-utils（模式 B） |
181	| processor 级 `size` 字典 | `processor.image_processor.size` 等 | 该 processor 处理的所有输入 | processor 内部（模式 A，或模式 B 未关 resize 时） |
182	
183	两层不要同时「较劲」：走模式 B 时预算交给 utils、processor 关掉 resize；走模式 A 时统一由 `size` 说了算。
184	
185	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
186	
187	图像（32× 空间压缩）：
188	
189	\[
190	N_{\text{img}} = \frac{H' \times W'}{32 \times 32}, \qquad
191	\text{shortest\_edge} \le H' \times W' \le \text{longest\_edge}
192	\]
193	
194	视频（32× 空间 + 2× 时间压缩，u2-l3 讲过帧数取偶正源于此）：
195	
196	\[
197	N_{\text{vid}} = \frac{T' \times H' \times W'}{32 \times 32 \times 2}
198	= \frac{T'}{2} \times \frac{H'}{32} \times \frac{W'}{32}, \qquad
199	\text{shortest\_edge} \le T' \times H' \times W' \le \text{longest\_edge}
200	\]
201	
202	反过来，**按目标 token 数配置预算**就用乘法（这就是官方示例数字的由来）：
203	
204	\[
205	\text{image size} = N_{\text{img}} \times 32 \times 32, \qquad
206	\text{video size} = N_{\text{vid}} \times 32 \times 32 \times 2
207	\]
208	
209	操作流程：
210	
211	```text
212	1. AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(ckpt)
213	2. processor.image_processor.size = {"longest_edge": N_max*32*32, "shortest_edge": N_min*32*32}
214	   processor.video_processor.size = {"longest_edge": N_max*32*32*2, "shortest_edge": N_min*32*32*2}
215	3. （可选）apply_chat_template(..., fps=...) 或 (..., num_frames=..., fps=None) 控制视频采样
216	4. 之后所有 tokenize=True 的调用都按新预算执行
217	```
218

280	### 4.3 add_vision_id：多模态输入自动编号
281	
282	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
283	
284	默认渲染下，图像/视频内容是「裸」地嵌进对话的。多图多轮对话中，用户说「第二张图里的狗」，模型只能靠位置隐式推断「第二张」是哪个。`add_vision_id=True` 让模板在每个视觉块前自动插入一段**普通文本编号**（`Picture N: ` / `Video N: `），把隐式的位置信息显式化——用户与模型从此有了一个共同的指代锚点。

351	### 4.4 batch 推理与左填充
352	
353	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
354	
355	batch 推理把多条样本的 `input_ids` 叠成一个矩形张量 \([B, L_{\max}]\)，但各样本长度天然不同，必须补齐（padding）。**关键约定：生成式模型必须左填充**——新生成 token 是接在每条序列**末尾**续写的，若把 pad 补在右侧，pad 会插在「提示结束」与「新生成」之间，模型把无意义的 pad 当成待续写内容；补在左侧则所有样本的真实内容都在序列右端对齐，`generate` 从同一位置起续写。
356	
357	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
358	
359	```text
360	两条样本（长度 12 与 35，pad_token 记为 PAD）
361	右填充（错误示范）:  [c₁..c₁₂  PAD PAD ... PAD]   ← 新 token 会生成在 PAD 之后
362	左填充（正确）:      [PAD PAD ... PAD c₁..c₁₂]   ← 真实内容右端对齐
363	                     [c₂₁ ... c₂₃₅            ]
364	
365	attention_mask 与 input_ids 同形：pad 位置为 0，真实 token 为 1（左填充 ⇒ 每行 0 集中在开头）
366	裁剪依然成立: generated_ids[i] 的前 L_max 个是输入（含 pad），
367	             out_ids[len(in_ids):] 依旧正确裁掉整个输入前缀
368	```
369	
370	注意一个容易忽略的事实：**batch 里可以混合多模态样本与纯文本样本**——视觉张量沿 batch 维独立拼接，文本侧的 padding 完全不干扰 `pixel_values` / `image_grid_thw`。
371	
372	#### 4.4.3 源码精读
373	
374	**左填充的两行设置**（[README.md:L292-L293](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L292-L293)）：L292 注释直言「batch generation 必须 left」，L293 `processor.tokenizer.padding_side = 'left'`——注意改的是 **tokenizer** 的属性（padding 由 tokenizer 执行，见 [web_demo_mm.py:L228](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/web_demo_mm.py#L228) 中 processor 持有 tokenizer 的三合一结构）。
375	
376	**混合模态 batch 的样本构造**（[README.md:L296-L311](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L296-L311)）：`messages1` 含两张图，`messages2` 是带 system 轮的**纯文本**对话；L311 `messages = [messages1, messages2]` 组成「列表的列表」——外层是 batch 维，内层才是一条对话。
377	
378	**调用时的 `padding=True`**（[README.md:L314-L321](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L314-L321)）：L320 在 `apply_chat_template` 里显式传 `padding=True`（L320 行内注释：batch generation 必须设置）。**设了 `padding_side` 却忘传 `padding=True`（或反之）都会让 batch 失效**，两者是一对。
379	
380	**裁剪与解码对 batch 的兼容**（[README.md:L325-L332](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L325-L332)）：与单样本完全同款的 `zip(inputs.input_ids, generated_ids)` + `out_ids[len(in_ids):]`——左填充下每条 `len(in_ids)` 都等于 \( L_{\max} \)，逐样本裁剪天然正确，无需任何改动。
381	
382	#### 4.4.4 代码实践
383	
384	1. **实践目标**：观察左填充在张量上的真实形态，验证裁剪逻辑不受 padding 影响。
385	2. **操作步骤**（示例代码；最后一步生成可选，只看张量可跳过加载模型）：
386	
387	```python
388	# 示例代码：u3_l1_practice_d.py
389	from transformers import AutoProcessor
390	
391	processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct")
392	processor.tokenizer.padding_side = "left"          # 设置一：方向
393	
394	messages1 = [{"role": "user", "content": [
395	    {"type": "image", "image": "/path/to/a.jpg"},
396	    {"type": "text", "text": "What is in this picture?"}]}]
397	messages2 = [{"role": "user", "content": [
398	    {"type": "text", "text": "Who are you?"}]}]
399	
400	inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
401	    [messages1, messages2],                        # 外层 = batch 维
402	    tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True,
403	    return_dict=True, return_tensors="pt",
404	    padding=True,                                  # 设置二：开关（与设置一成对）
405	)
406	print("input_ids:", inputs["input_ids"].shape)
407	print("attention_mask 每行前 8 个:", inputs["attention_mask"][:, :8])
408	print("每行 padding 个数:", (inputs["attention_mask"] == 0).sum(dim=1).tolist())
409	pad_id = processor.tokenizer.pad_token_id
410	print("pad_token:", processor.tokenizer.pad_token, "开头是否为 pad:",
411	      (inputs["input_ids"][:, 0] == pad_id).tolist())
412	```
413	
414	3. **需要观察的现象**：`attention_mask` 的 0 **全部集中在每行开头**；较短样本（纯文本那条）所在行的 0 更多；`input_ids` 每行长度相同（等于 batch 内最长序列）。
415	4. **预期结果**：若再加载模型执行 `model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=32)` 并用 `out_ids[len(in_ids):]` 裁剪，两条输出都应是干净的新生成文本、不含 pad 与提示词。具体 pad 数量取决于两条样本的长度差，**待本地验证**。
416	
417	#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案
418	
419	**练习 1**：只用 `padding=True` 而不改 `padding_side`，最可能看到什么现象？
420	答案：tokenizer 默认右填充，pad 补在序列右侧。生成会把 pad 当成提示的一部分续写下去，输出常以无意义内容开头，甚至永不命中结束符；同时「真实提示右端对齐」被破坏。
421	
422	**练习 2**：左填充后，`inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]` 对两条样本分别意味着什么？
423	答案：都等于 batch 内最长序列的长度 \( L_{\max} \)——含 pad。因此逐样本 `len(in_ids)` 相同，`out_ids[len(in_ids):]` 恰好裁掉「pad + 提示」的完整输入前缀。
424	
425	**练习 3**：batch 中一条含 2 张图、一条纯文本，`pixel_values` 会为纯文本样本补空张量吗？
426	答案：不会。视觉张量只按实际存在的图像拼接（`image_grid_thw` 逐图记录网格），文本侧 padding 与视觉侧互不相干——[README.md:L296-L311](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L296-L311) 的官方 batch 示例正是这种混合模态组合。
427	
428	## 5. 综合实践
429	
430	**任务：写一个 `processor_probe.py` 体检脚本，产出一份《processor 行为笔记》。** 把本讲四个模块串成一个可复跑的脚本，对**同一组 messages**（1 张高分辨率图片 + 1 段提问）依次完成：
431	
432	1. **渲染检查**（4.1）：`tokenize=False` 打印提示串，人工标注 `<|im_start|>` / `<|vision_start|>` / `<|image_pad|>` / `<|im_end|>` 各出现几次。
433	2. **展开验证**（4.1 + 4.2）：`tokenize=True` 下统计 `input_ids` 中 `<|image_pad|>` 的个数，与 `image_grid_thw` 三元素乘积对照，再验证乘积 × 1024（像素数）落在当前预算区间内。
434	3. **预算对照**（4.2）：分别在「默认预算」与 `{"longest_edge": 1280*32*32, "shortest_edge": 256*32*32}` 两档下记录 `input_ids` 长度与视觉 token 数，写进 `notes.md` 的表格，并用一句话解释长度差来源。
435	4. **编号对照**（4.3）：把 messages 扩成「2 图 + 1 视频占位」的多轮对话，`add_vision_id` 两种取值各渲染一次，把 diff 行摘进笔记。
436	5. **batch 检查**（4.4）：把（多模态样本，纯文本样本）组成 batch，`padding_side='left'` + `padding=True`，记录 `input_ids` 形状与每行 padding 数。
437	
438	**验收标准**：`notes.md` 中应能回答——这张图在你的默认预算下占多少视觉 token？改预算后 `input_ids` 长度变化了多少、差值是否恰等于视觉 token 数之差？左填充的 0 在张量的哪一侧？全部结论都来自你自己的运行输出（本环境无 GPU/未装 transformers，结果**待本地验证**）。
439	
440	## 6. 本讲小结
441	
442	- `apply_chat_template` 有两种模式：`tokenize=True` 一步返回含 `pixel_values` / `image_grid_thw` 的张量（transformers 路径）；`tokenize=False` 只返回字符串、每个图像仅 1 个 `<|image_pad|>` 占位（配合 qwen-vl-utils + `do_resize=False`，或交给 vLLM）。web_demo_mm.py 的两个后端分支就是两种模式的活样本。
443	- `<|image_pad|>` 在编码阶段展开为 \( \frac{H'}{32} \times \frac{W'}{32} \) 个，因此 **size 预算 → 图像实际尺寸 → input_ids 长度**是一条因果链。
444	- processor 级预算分治：`image_processor.size` 的 longest/shortest_edge 约束**单图** \( H \times W \)；`video_processor.size` 约束**全帧总和** \( T \times H \times W \)；按目标 token 数配置时分别乘 \( 32 \times 32 \) 与 \( 32 \times 32 \times 2 \)。
445	- `add_vision_id=True` 在每个视觉块前插入普通文本编号（图像 `Picture N`、视频 `Video N` 独立累加，跨轮不断档），为多图对话提供显式指代锚点。
446	- batch 推理两件套缺一不可：`processor.tokenizer.padding_side = 'left'` + `padding=True`；左填充让真实内容右端对齐，pad 位置 `attention_mask=0`，逐样本 `out_ids[len(in_ids):]` 裁剪无需任何修改，且 batch 可混排多模态与纯文本样本。
447	
448	## 7. 下一步学习建议

452	- 想理解 `image_grid_thw` 里的网格如何变成 3D 位置 id：预习单元五的 rope2d.py（u5-l4），那是本仓库中最接近模型内部机制的源码。

# 深入 processor：chat template、像素预算与 add_vision_id

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 读懂 `apply_chat_template` 两种模式（`tokenize=False` / `tokenize=True`）各自的输出形态与内部流水线，说清 `<|image_pad|>` 从「一个占位符」到「N 个 token」的展开发生在哪一步、N 由什么决定。
2. 掌握 `processor.image_processor.size` 与 `processor.video_processor.size` 两套像素预算的**语义差异**（单帧预算 vs 全帧总预算），能按目标视觉 token 数反推出 size 取值，并说清它与 u2-l2 元素级预算的分层关系。
3. 会用 `add_vision_id=True` 为多图/多视频对话自动加上「Picture N: / Video N:」编号，并知道编号文本在提示串里的确切位置。
4. 掌握 batch 推理的两个必备设置——`processor.tokenizer.padding_side = 'left'` 与 `padding=True`——并能解释左填充与输出裁剪 `out_ids[len(in_ids):]` 为什么能配合工作。

u1-l3 已经建立了「apply_chat_template → generate → 裁剪解码」的调用链骨架，并在实践中粗看了一眼两种模式的类型差异；本讲把 processor 这一环拆开细讲，所有实践**只需 processor、不需加载模型权重**，笔记本电脑 CPU 即可完成。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 承接前讲：两条已有结论

- **u1-l3**：`processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, return_dict=True, return_tensors="pt")` 一步返回 `BatchEncoding`，其中除了 `input_ids` / `attention_mask`，还有 `pixel_values`、`image_grid_thw`（视频输入时是 `pixel_values_videos` / `video_grid_thw` 等时间戳张量）。
- **u2-l2**：qwen-vl-utils 在 **messages 元素级** 提供 `min_pixels` / `max_pixels` 预算，图像宽高被对齐到 32 的倍数，视觉 token 数 \( N = \frac{H}{32} \times \frac{W}{32} \)。

本讲要回答的追问是：**transformers 的 processor 内部还有一套预算（`size` 字典），它和 qwen-vl-utils 那套是什么关系？谁在什么时候生效？**

### 2.2 AutoProcessor：三合一的预处理入口

`AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(...)` 加载的不是单一对象，而是三个组件的组合：

| 组件 | 访问方式 | 职责 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tokenizer | `processor.tokenizer` | 文本 ↔ token id，负责 padding |
| image_processor | `processor.image_processor` | 图像加载、缩放（执行 size 预算）、patch 化，持有 `patch_size` |
| video_processor | `processor.video_processor` | 视频帧采样与缩放（执行视频 size 预算） |

README 明确说明 Qwen3-VL 的 processor **把图像与视频处理拆成了两个独立组件**，因此两种模态可以各配一套预算（[README.md:L339](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L339)）。另外，`processor.image_processor.patch_size` 是 patch 边长的**权威来源**——u2-l1 说过「Qwen3-VL 必须传 `image_patch_size=16`，最佳实践是动态读取」，本讲 4.2.3 会看到 web_demo_mm.py 里那句动态读取的真实出处。

### 2.3 Qwen3-VL 提示串中的特殊 token 速查

以下是 README 官方给出的渲染结果中出现的全部特殊 token（出处见 4.3.3 的 [README.md:L729](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L729)）：

| token | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| `<\|im_start\|>` / `<\|im_end\|>` | 对话轮次的开始 / 结束包裹符，后跟 `system` / `user` / `assistant` 角色名 |
| `<\|vision_start\|>` / `<\|vision_end\|>` | 一个视觉输入块的包裹符（图像与视频通用） |
| `<\|image_pad\|>` | 图像占位 token（编码阶段按视觉 token 数展开） |
| `<\|video_pad\|>` | 视频占位 token（同样按视觉 token 数展开） |

### 2.4 实验环境

- transformers ≥ 4.57.0（[README.md:L132-L135](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L132-L135)），建议用 `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` 做实验（processor 与大模型同构，但更省流量）。
- 本讲实践中 `apply_chat_template` 只用 processor 做预处理，**无需 `AutoModelForImageTextToText`**；只有 4.4 的最后一步「跑一次 batch 生成」可选地需要模型（也可只检查张量形状跳过生成）。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 本讲关注的行段 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [README.md](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md) | L177-L183 模式 A 调用；L288-L334 batch 推理；L336-L356 像素预算语义与代码；L358-L397 fps/num_frames；L436 与 L527-L532 模式 B 组合调用；L688-L738 add_vision_id | 官方对 processor 全部用法约定的「规范文本」 |
| [web_demo_mm.py](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/web_demo_mm.py) | L180 与 L220-L226 两种 tokenize 模式的真实分工；L183 patch_size 动态读取；L178-L198 `_prepare_inputs_for_vllm` | 仓库中唯一同时用上两种模式的可运行工程代码 |

说明：processor 的**实现代码**（chat template Jinja 模板、`Qwen3VLImageProcessor` 的 resize 逻辑）位于 transformers 库与模型仓库中，不在本仓库——本讲的源码精读以本仓库的官方文档与工程用法为锚点，行为断言均可被 4.x 的实践在本地验证。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 apply_chat_template 的两种模式

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`apply_chat_template` 有两种工作模式，区别在于「模板渲染」与「视觉预处理 + 分词编码」是否一步完成：

- **模式 A：一步到位（`tokenize=True`）**。渲染对话模板的同时，processor 自动完成图像/视频加载、按预算缩放、patch 化，并把每个视觉占位符展开成与视觉 token 数一致的 `<|image_pad|>` / `<|video_pad|>`，最终返回 `input_ids` + `pixel_values` 等张量。这是 **transformers 推理的默认路径**。
- **模式 B：渲染与编码分离（`tokenize=False`）**。只做模板渲染，返回**纯字符串**：每个图像位置只留**一个** `<|image_pad|>` 占位符。视觉部分交给外部工具（qwen-vl-utils）处理，再由 `processor(text=..., images=..., videos=..., do_resize=False)` 显式编码。这是 **vLLM / 自定义预处理场景的路径**。

为什么需要模式 B？因为 qwen-vl-utils 已经按元素级预算完成缩放与帧采样（u2-l2 / u2-l3），若让 processor 再 resize 一次，既浪费算力又可能破坏已对齐的尺寸，所以要传 `do_resize=False`；而 vLLM 引擎接收的是「原始 prompt 字符串 + 张量字典」，编码由引擎内部完成（这正是 u3-l2 的主角）。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```text
模式 A（tokenize=True，一步到位）
  messages ──渲染模板──▶ 含 <|image_pad|> 占位的提示串
          ──processor 加载图像并按 size 预算缩放（H',W' 对齐 32）──▶ pixel_values + 网格
          ──把占位符展开为 (H'/32)×(W'/32) 个 <|image_pad|>，分词──▶ input_ids
          ──返回──▶ BatchEncoding{input_ids, attention_mask, pixel_values, image_grid_thw, ...}

模式 B（tokenize=False，渲染/编码分离）
  messages ──渲染模板──▶ 纯字符串 text（每个图像仅 1 个 <|image_pad|>）
          ──qwen_vl_utils.process_vision_info──▶ 已缩放的图像/视频张量 + video_kwargs
          ──processor(text=text, images=..., videos=..., do_resize=False)──▶ 同样的 BatchEncoding
          （或把 text + 张量直接交给 vLLM 引擎）
```

两条路殊途同归，但有一条**因果链**值得背下来：

\[ \text{size 预算} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{缩放后尺寸 } H' \times W' \;\Rightarrow\; \text{视觉 token 数 } \tfrac{H'}{32} \times \tfrac{W'}{32} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{input\_ids 长度} \]

这就是为什么 4.2 的预算实验直接表现为「`input_ids` 变长/变短」。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**模式 A 的标准调用**（[README.md:L177-L183](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L177-L183)）：这段是官方 Quickstart 的预处理调用，`tokenize=True` + `return_dict=True` + `return_tensors="pt"` 三件套，messages 里的图像 URL 由 processor 自行下载。

**模式 B 的标准组合拳**（[README.md:L527-L532](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L527-L532)）：L527 用 `tokenize=False` 拿到字符串，L528 用 `process_vision_info(messages, image_patch_size=16)` 得到已缩放的图像，L532 把两者交给 `processor(text=..., images=..., videos=..., do_resize=False, return_tensors="pt")` 完成**编码**。注意 L530-L531 的注释与 [README.md:L436](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L436) 的📌提示：**utils 已缩放过，processor 必须 `do_resize=False` 以避免二次缩放**——这句话就是两套预算的「交接协议」。

**两种模式在一个真实工程文件里的分工**（[web_demo_mm.py:L180](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/web_demo_mm.py#L180) 与 [web_demo_mm.py:L220-L226](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/web_demo_mm.py#L220-L226)）：

- vLLM 分支的 `_prepare_inputs_for_vllm` 用 `tokenize=False` 只取提示串（L180），因为张量要原样交给 vLLM 引擎；
- HF 分支的 `call_local_model` 用 `tokenize=True` 一步拿到全部输入张量直接 `model.generate`（L220-L226，u1-l4 已讲过该分支的流式线程）。

同一个函数族、同一个 messages，两种模式的选择完全由**后端吃什么样的输入**决定——这是本讲最重要的工程直觉。

**`add_generation_prompt=True` 渲染出了什么**：对照 [README.md:L729](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L729) 给出的预期串，末尾是 `<|im_start|>assistant\n`——即「助手轮的开头」。模型从这里续写回答，`batch_decode(skip_special_tokens=True)` 时最终又把它过滤掉。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

1. **实践目标**：亲眼确认两种模式的输出形态，并数出 `<|image_pad|>` 的个数与其决定因素。
2. **操作步骤**（示例代码，只需 processor）：

```python
# 示例代码：u3_l1_practice_a.py
from transformers import AutoProcessor

ckpt = "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct"
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(ckpt)

messages = [{
    "role": "user",
    "content": [
        {"type": "image", "image": "https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-VL/assets/demo.jpeg"},
        {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."},
    ],
}]

# 模式 B：只渲染
text = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
print(repr(text))                      # 观察 <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|> 的个数
print("字符串中 image_pad 个数:", text.count("<|image_pad|>"))

# 模式 A：一步到位
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
    messages, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True,
    return_dict=True, return_tensors="pt",
)
print(inputs.keys())
print("input_ids 形状:", inputs["input_ids"].shape)

pid = processor.tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids("<|image_pad|>")
n_pad = (inputs["input_ids"] == pid).sum().item()
grid = inputs["image_grid_thw"][0]     # (t, h, w)
print("input_ids 中 image_pad 个数:", n_pad)
print("image_grid_thw:", grid.tolist(), "乘积:", grid.prod().item())
```

3. **需要观察的现象**：字符串里每个图像只有 **1 个** `<|image_pad|>`；而 `input_ids` 里它是成片出现的，个数恰好等于 `image_grid_thw` 的三元素乘积 \( t \times h \times w \)（图像 \( t=1 \)，即 \( \frac{H'}{32} \times \frac{W'}{32} \)）。
4. **预期结果**：`n_pad == grid.prod().item()` 成立；把 `inputs["input_ids"]` 用 `processor.tokenizer.decode` 解码后与 `text` 逐字符对齐（唯一差异是占位符个数）。具体的 token 数取决于 demo.jpeg 在默认预算下的缩放结果，**待本地验证**。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：模式 B 里，如果把 `do_resize=False` 忘了传，会发生什么？
答案：processor 的 image_processor 会对 utils 已缩放好的图像**再执行一次** size 预算缩放。轻则浪费算力，重则当 processor 预算与 utils 预算不一致时图像被二次缩放，`image_grid_thw` 与 utils 意图不符（官方在 [README.md:L436](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L436) 专门加了📌提示）。

**练习 2**：为什么 vLLM 分支用 `tokenize=False` 而不是 `tokenize=True` 后再把张量拆出来？
答案：vLLM 的输入协议是「prompt 字符串 + `multi_modal_data` 张量字典 + `mm_processor_kwargs`」（见 [web_demo_mm.py:L194-L198](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/web_demo_mm.py#L194-L198)），编码由引擎内部的 processor 完成；自己先编码反而会丢失「按引擎侧预算展开占位符」的机会。

**练习 3**：`add_generation_prompt=True` 渲染出的最后一个 token 是什么？为什么 `batch_decode` 看不到它？
答案：`<|im_start|>assistant\n` 对应的 token；`batch_decode(..., skip_special_tokens=True)` 会过滤特殊 token，所以最终输出文本里不出现。

### 4.2 size 预算参数：image_processor 与 video_processor 的分治

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

processor 级预算写在两个 `size` 字典里，**图像与视频语义不同**是本节最大的坑：

- `processor.image_processor.size = {"longest_edge": ..., "shortest_edge": ...}`
  - `longest_edge` 对应 `max_pixels`：**单张图**的 \( H \times W \) 上限；
  - `shortest_edge` 对应 `min_pixels`：单张图像素下限（[README.md:L341-L342](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L341-L342)）。
- `processor.video_processor.size = {"longest_edge": ..., "shortest_edge": ...}`
  - `longest_edge` 是**全部帧的像素总和**上限：视频形状为 \( T \times H \times W \) 时，\( T \times H \times W \) 不得超过它；`shortest_edge` 是总预算下限（[README.md:L345-L346](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L345-L346)）。

它与 u2-l2 元素级预算构成**两层旋钮**：

| 层次 | 写在哪 | 作用域 | 生效路径 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 元素级 `min_pixels` / `max_pixels` / `total_pixels` | messages 的 image/video 元素里 | 单个输入 | qwen-vl-utils（模式 B） |
| processor 级 `size` 字典 | `processor.image_processor.size` 等 | 该 processor 处理的所有输入 | processor 内部（模式 A，或模式 B 未关 resize 时） |

两层不要同时「较劲」：走模式 B 时预算交给 utils、processor 关掉 resize；走模式 A 时统一由 `size` 说了算。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

图像（32× 空间压缩）：

\[
N_{\text{img}} = \frac{H' \times W'}{32 \times 32}, \qquad
\text{shortest\_edge} \le H' \times W' \le \text{longest\_edge}
\]

视频（32× 空间 + 2× 时间压缩，u2-l3 讲过帧数取偶正源于此）：

\[
N_{\text{vid}} = \frac{T' \times H' \times W'}{32 \times 32 \times 2}
= \frac{T'}{2} \times \frac{H'}{32} \times \frac{W'}{32}, \qquad
\text{shortest\_edge} \le T' \times H' \times W' \le \text{longest\_edge}
\]

反过来，**按目标 token 数配置预算**就用乘法（这就是官方示例数字的由来）：

\[
\text{image size} = N_{\text{img}} \times 32 \times 32, \qquad
\text{video size} = N_{\text{vid}} \times 32 \times 32 \times 2
\]

操作流程：

```text
1. AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(ckpt)
2. processor.image_processor.size = {"longest_edge": N_max*32*32, "shortest_edge": N_min*32*32}
   processor.video_processor.size = {"longest_edge": N_max*32*32*2, "shortest_edge": N_min*32*32*2}
3. （可选）apply_chat_template(..., fps=...) 或 (..., num_frames=..., fps=None) 控制视频采样
4. 之后所有 tokenize=True 的调用都按新预算执行
```

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**官方预算配置代码**（[README.md:L349-L356](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L349-L356)）：L352 给 image_processor 设 `{"longest_edge": 1280*32*32, "shortest_edge": 256*32*32}`——L351 注释点破换算：32 倍压缩下，这等于**单张图 256～1280 个视觉 token**；L355 给 video_processor 设 `{"longest_edge": 16384*32*32*2, "shortest_edge": 256*32*32*2}`——L354 注释说明是「32× 空间 + 2× 时间压缩」，即**单视频 256～16384 个 token**。注意赋值是**整体替换** size 字典，两个键都要写全。

**视频采样参数直传 processor**（[README.md:L358-L397](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L358-L397)）：L374-L375 注释说明默认 `fps=2`；L378-L385 示范在 `apply_chat_template` 调用里直接传 `fps=4`；L388-L397 示范 `num_frames=128` 并**同时显式传 `fps=None`** 覆盖之（帧数采样公式本身在 u2-l3 的 `smart_nframes` 已拆解，processor 内部是同一套逻辑的 processor 侧入口）。这组参数只在模式 A / processor 路径下生效；模式 B 的采样由 utils 的 `video_kwargs`（`do_sample_frames=False`）接管。

### 4.3 add_vision_id：多模态输入自动编号

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

默认渲染下，图像/视频内容是「裸」地嵌进对话的。多图多轮对话中，用户说「第二张图里的狗」，模型只能靠位置隐式推断「第二张」是哪个。`add_vision_id=True` 让模板在每个视觉块前自动插入一段**普通文本编号**（`Picture N: ` / `Video N: `），把隐式的位置信息显式化——用户与模型从此有了一个共同的指代锚点。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

编号规则（由官方示例的预期输出可直接读出）：

- 图像序列独立编号：`Picture 1`、`Picture 2`、`Picture 3`……跨轮次**持续累加**，不因新开一轮而重新计数；
- 视频序列独立编号：`Video 1`、`Video 2`……与图像计数互不干扰；
- 编号文本插在 `<|vision_start|>` **之前**、属于提示串的普通文本 token（不是特殊 token）。

```text
content: [text, image, image, video, text]
默认:    text <vis_start><image_pad><vis_end> <vis_start><image_pad><vis_end> <vis_start><video_pad><vis_end> text
加编号:  text Picture 1: <vis_start>... Picture 2: <vis_start>... Video 1: <vis_start>... text
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**功能说明**（[README.md:L690-L691](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L690-L691)）：官方定位——默认图像与视频内容直接嵌入对话，处理多图时加标签便于指代，行为由用户开关控制。

**两种渲染的预期输出对照**（[README.md:L725-L729](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L725-L729) 默认 vs [README.md:L732-L736](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L732-L736) `add_vision_id=True`）：L736 的串里可以看到 `Picture 1: <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>`、`Picture 2: ... Picture 3: ... Video 1: <|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>`——首个 user 轮的图是 Picture 1，第二个 user 轮的两张图接着是 Picture 2、3，视频单独从 Video 1 起数。

### 4.4 batch 推理与左填充

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

batch 推理把多条样本的 `input_ids` 叠成一个矩形张量 \([B, L_{\max}]\)，但各样本长度天然不同，必须补齐（padding）。**关键约定：生成式模型必须左填充**——新生成 token 是接在每条序列**末尾**续写的，若把 pad 补在右侧，pad 会插在「提示结束」与「新生成」之间，模型把无意义的 pad 当成待续写内容；补在左侧则所有样本的真实内容都在序列右端对齐，`generate` 从同一位置起续写。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```text
两条样本（长度 12 与 35，pad_token 记为 PAD）
右填充（错误示范）:  [c₁..c₁₂  PAD PAD ... PAD]   ← 新 token 会生成在 PAD 之后
左填充（正确）:      [PAD PAD ... PAD c₁..c₁₂]   ← 真实内容右端对齐
                     [c₂₁ ... c₂₃₅            ]

attention_mask 与 input_ids 同形：pad 位置为 0，真实 token 为 1（左填充 ⇒ 每行 0 集中在开头）
裁剪依然成立: generated_ids[i] 的前 L_max 个是输入（含 pad），

```

注意一个容易忽略的事实：**batch 里可以混合多模态样本与纯文本样本**——视觉张量沿 batch 维独立拼接，文本侧的 padding 完全不干扰 `pixel_values` / `image_grid_thw`。

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

**左填充的两行设置**（[README.md:L292-L293](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L292-L293)）：L292 注释直言「batch generation 必须 left」，L293 `processor.tokenizer.padding_side = 'left'`——注意改的是 **tokenizer** 的属性（padding 由 tokenizer 执行，见 [web_demo_mm.py:L228](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/web_demo_mm.py#L228) 中 processor 持有 tokenizer 的三合一结构）。

**混合模态 batch 的样本构造**（[README.md:L296-L311](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L296-L311)）：`messages1` 含两张图，`messages2` 是带 system 轮的**纯文本**对话；L311 `messages = [messages1, messages2]` 组成「列表的列表」——外层是 batch 维，内层才是一条对话。

**调用时的 `padding=True`**（[README.md:L314-L321](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L314-L321)）：L320 在 `apply_chat_template` 里显式传 `padding=True`（L320 行内注释：batch generation 必须设置）。**设了 `padding_side` 却忘传 `padding=True`（或反之）都会让 batch 失效**，两者是一对。

**裁剪与解码对 batch 的兼容**（[README.md:L325-L332](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L325-L332)）：与单样本完全同款的 `zip(inputs.input_ids, generated_ids)` + `out_ids[len(in_ids):]`——左填充下每条 `len(in_ids)` 都等于 \( L_{\max} \)，逐样本裁剪天然正确，无需任何改动。

#### 4.4.4 代码实践

1. **实践目标**：观察左填充在张量上的真实形态，验证裁剪逻辑不受 padding 影响。
2. **操作步骤**（示例代码；最后一步生成可选，只看张量可跳过加载模型）：

```python
# 示例代码：u3_l1_practice_d.py
from transformers import AutoProcessor

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct")
processor.tokenizer.padding_side = "left"          # 设置一：方向

messages1 = [{"role": "user", "content": [
    {"type": "image", "image": "/path/to/a.jpg"},
    {"type": "text", "text": "What is in this picture?"}]}]
messages2 = [{"role": "user", "content": [
    {"type": "text", "text": "Who are you?"}]}]

inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
    [messages1, messages2],                        # 外层 = batch 维
    tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True,
    return_dict=True, return_tensors="pt",
    padding=True,                                  # 设置二：开关（与设置一成对）
)
print("input_ids:", inputs["input_ids"].shape)
print("attention_mask 每行前 8 个:", inputs["attention_mask"][:, :8])
print("每行 padding 个数:", (inputs["attention_mask"] == 0).sum(dim=1).tolist())
pad_id = processor.tokenizer.pad_token_id
print("pad_token:", processor.tokenizer.pad_token, "开头是否为 pad:",
      (inputs["input_ids"][:, 0] == pad_id).tolist())
```

3. **需要观察的现象**：`attention_mask` 的 0 **全部集中在每行开头**；较短样本（纯文本那条）所在行的 0 更多；`input_ids` 每行长度相同（等于 batch 内最长序列）。
4. **预期结果**：若再加载模型执行 `model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=32)` 并用 `out_ids[len(in_ids):]` 裁剪，两条输出都应是干净的新生成文本、不含 pad 与提示词。具体 pad 数量取决于两条样本的长度差，**待本地验证**。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：只用 `padding=True` 而不改 `padding_side`，最可能看到什么现象？
答案：tokenizer 默认右填充，pad 补在序列右侧。生成会把 pad 当成提示的一部分续写下去，输出常以无意义内容开头，甚至永不命中结束符；同时「真实提示右端对齐」被破坏。

**练习 2**：左填充后，`inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]` 对两条样本分别意味着什么？

**练习 3**：batch 中一条含 2 张图、一条纯文本，`pixel_values` 会为纯文本样本补空张量吗？

## 5. 综合实践

**任务：写一个 `processor_probe.py` 体检脚本，产出一份《processor 行为笔记》。** 把本讲四个模块串成一个可复跑的脚本，对**同一组 messages**（1 张高分辨率图片 + 1 段提问）依次完成：

1. **渲染检查**（4.1）：`tokenize=False` 打印提示串，人工标注 `<|im_start|>` / `<|vision_start|>` / `<|image_pad|>` / `<|im_end|>` 各出现几次。
2. **展开验证**（4.1 + 4.2）：`tokenize=True` 下统计 `input_ids` 中 `<|image_pad|>` 的个数，与 `image_grid_thw` 三元素乘积对照，再验证乘积 × 1024（像素数）落在当前预算区间内。
3. **预算对照**（4.2）：分别在「默认预算」与 `{"longest_edge": 1280*32*32, "shortest_edge": 256*32*32}` 两档下记录 `input_ids` 长度与视觉 token 数，写进 `notes.md` 的表格，并用一句话解释长度差来源。
4. **编号对照**（4.3）：把 messages 扩成「2 图 + 1 视频占位」的多轮对话，`add_vision_id` 两种取值各渲染一次，把 diff 行摘进笔记。
5. **batch 检查**（4.4）：把（多模态样本，纯文本样本）组成 batch，`padding_side='left'` + `padding=True`，记录 `input_ids` 形状与每行 padding 数。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `apply_chat_template` 有两种模式：`tokenize=True` 一步返回含 `pixel_values` / `image_grid_thw` 的张量（transformers 路径）；`tokenize=False` 只返回字符串、每个图像仅 1 个 `<|image_pad|>` 占位（配合 qwen-vl-utils + `do_resize=False`，或交给 vLLM）。web_demo_mm.py 的两个后端分支就是两种模式的活样本。

- processor 级预算分治：`image_processor.size` 的 longest/shortest_edge 约束**单图** \( H \times W \)；`video_processor.size` 约束**全帧总和** \( T \times H \times W \)；按目标 token 数配置时分别乘 \( 32 \times 32 \) 与 \( 32 \times 32 \times 2 \)。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

- **下一讲 u3-l2（vLLM 离线推理与 prepare_inputs_for_vllm 模式）**：本讲模式 B 的终点正是它的起点——`prompt` / `multi_modal_data` / `mm_processor_kwargs` 三件套如何在 vLLM 引擎里落地，建议先精读 [web_demo_mm.py:L178-L198](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/web_demo_mm.py#L178-L198) 带着问题过去。
- 想看 processor 的**实现**（chat template 的 Jinja 模板、`Qwen3VLImageProcessor` 的 resize 细节）：读本机安装的 transformers ≥ 4.57.0 源码中 `models/qwen3_vl/` 目录与模型仓库里的 `chat_template.json`、`preprocessor_config.json`，对照本讲的行为断言逐条验证。
- 想理解 `image_grid_thw` 里的网格如何变成 3D 位置 id：预习单元五的 rope2d.py（u5-l4），那是本仓库中最接近模型内部机制的源码。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
